pos.personaBrief: Ultradefensivo-mordedor team (El Gráfico 1967) that won through rehearsed set pieces and pressing without the ball; possession has no verified fact and the team never sought it for its own sake.

pro.personaBrief: Quick forwards chasing rivals, switches of play for the man attacking behind the defense (Manera 1967) and Pachamé as a destroyer point to direct, safe, vertical play rather than patient build-up.

est.personaBrief: Everyone had to fulfil all functions and forwards crossed constantly, Verón swapped wings and Ribaudo drifted from nine; yet movements were drilled in the laboratory, so structure is relational but rehearsed.

lar.personaBrief: Manera's weekly switches of play and Verón/Ribaudo alternating flanks and corners to the first post show use of the wings, but with a central trio and two crossing forwards rather than classic touchline wingers.

blo.personaBrief: Forwards chased rivals to their own box, Trivela notes more midfield marking and the offside line, so the team defended high and aggressively, relying on rehearsed set pieces more than on high steals.

mar.personaBrief: Marcas personales and marca fija are documented repeatedly: Togneri on Charlton, Malbernat on the forward, Zubeldía the defender of personal marking.

pla.personaBrief: Zubeldía studied every rival and tailored marks (Togneri on Charlton), changed shirt numbers to confuse, but also imposed a drilled method and his authority on arrival.

res.personaBrief: Winning at any cost, delaying play and provocations, game-managing at Old Trafford with Bilardo; 'algunos partidos tienen 180 minutos' shows a result-first mentality.

sis.personaBrief: A humble squad turned champion through a collective system, long talks and drilled moves; everyone performed all functions, no free role for stars.

jog.personaBrief: Physical preparation, aerial set pieces ('dos cabezazos en el área son gol'), fierce challenges and Pachamé/Bilardo as workers; strong, intense athletes fit the team.

bas.personaBrief: Built on the killer juveniles of the Tercera (Ignomiriello) mixed with a few hand-picked signings, and the title was won with these young players.

lid.personaBrief: Zubeldía was the boss with long concentrations and strict control, taking blame publicly, though he discussed ideas in long talks until all were convinced.
